podcast.title: Severe Endometriosis Diagnosis (2016)
podcast.body: In 2016, Halsey was diagnosed with a severe case of endometriosis, a painful female reproductive disease that led to a miscarriage and required at least one surgery. "In 2016, she was diagnosed with a severe case of endometriosis, a female reproductive disease that could be very painful and something that caused a miscarriage. Her case is quite bad and has resulted in at least one round of surgery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "A Story Like Mine" – Spoken Word Performance (2018)
podcast.body: At the Women's March in New York City in March 2018, Halsey performed a powerful spoken word piece that recounted deeply personal and traumatic experiences of sexual assault and abuse from various stages of her life, and that of her friends, tying it into the broader #MeToo movement. She described a friend's rape at 14 in 2009, her own childhood experience in 2002 by a neighbor's son, a coercive relationship in 2012, and a later assault in 2017 despite believing she was "protected" by her fame. She also revealed performing a show in Chicago while having a miscarriage. The piece emphasized that "nobody is safe" as long as women are alive and acknowledged figures like Ashley, Simone, Gabby, Makayla, Gaga, and Rosario Alli as heroes. "It's Halsey. We're siding up home from a women's march in New York City in March 2018."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 4: (70-61)

podcast.title: ADHD Diagnosis
podcast.body: While undergoing treatment for bipolar disorder, Halsey discovered and sought help for ADHD. "When she was being treated for that, she also discovered she had ADHD. She sought help for that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bipolar Disorder Diagnosis (Age 17)
podcast.body: Halsey was diagnosed with bipolar disorder at 17, a condition that also affected her mother, and has been openly vocal about her struggles to raise understanding. "First, she was diagnosed as bipolar when she was 17, a condition that also plagued your mother."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Determination Against Illness
podcast.body: Despite dealing with a wide range of incurable health issues, Halsey is determined not to let any of these problems overcome her. "In other words, Halsey has a lot to deal with over a wide range of health issues, but she is determined not to let any of those problems get the best of her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome Diagnosis
podcast.body: Halsey has been diagnosed with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, a group of genetic connective tissue disorders characterized by loose, painful joints, very stretchy skin, and skin scarring. This condition can lead to further complications, including heart and nerve disorders, and is managed as there is no cure. "Halsey has also been diagnosed with Elyrs Danlow syndrome. This is a series of genetic connective tissue disorders that results in loose joints, painful joints, very stretchy skin and scarring of the skin. These conditions can lead to other problems in the body ranging from heart problems to nerve disorders and more. There's no cure, so it can only be managed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Gluten Intolerance
podcast.body: Halsey also suffers from a serious intolerance to gluten, adding to her complex health profile. "If that's not enough, she has a serious intolerance to gluten."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Health Conditions and Openness
podcast.body: Halsey has openly dealt with several health challenges throughout her life, including bipolar disorder since adolescence and ADHD during school. She has also discussed her experiences with miscarriage and endometriosis, and continues to manage a series of health conditions such as Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, Sjögren's Syndrome, and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome. "Halsey has dealt with bipolar disorders since she was a teenager. ADHD was a problem in school. Halsey has talked about her miscarriage and endometriosis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome Diagnosis
podcast.body: Another diagnosis for Halsey is Mast Cell Activation Syndrome, which presents as an extreme allergic reaction capable of causing problems in the heart, skin, stomach, and lungs. "Halsey also has mast cell activation syndrome, which is like having an extreme sort of allergy that can cause problems with the heart, skin, stomach and lungs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) Diagnosis
podcast.body: Halsey has Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), a heart condition that causes the heart to beat excessively fast merely by standing up. Symptoms include brain fog, fatigue, headaches, shaking, and even purple discoloration of the feet when upright. "And she has postural, orthostatic, tachycardia syndrome. That's a heart problem that can send the thing beating way too fast just by standing up. It results in brain fog, fatigue, headaches, shaking and even having your feet turned purple when you stand up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sjögren's Syndrome Diagnosis
podcast.body: Halsey also lives with Sjögren's syndrome, an autoimmune disease that can affect various body parts, from salivary glands to lungs and kidneys. "And I'm not done. Halsey also has Sorgyn syndrome, which is an autoimmune disease that can affect everything from the salivary glands to problems with the lungs and the kidneys and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Social Media Origin
podcast.body: Halsey is cited as an artist who rose to prominence and built her career through the use of social media platforms. "Halsey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)

podcast.title: Strong Artistic Control
podcast.body: Halsey is known for her assertive stance in her career, making it clear that she is not to be dictated to by her record company or external pressures. She maintains full control over her artistic and career decisions and strongly dislikes the concept of "forced viral moments." "Halsey is going to do what Halsey wants to do no matter what you're talking about."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Unique Identity and Influences
podcast.body: Halsey has synthesized various influences, including Jagger, Bowie, Amy Winehouse, and Dolores O'Riordan, to craft a distinctive identity. This identity incorporates concepts of gender identity, bisexuality, film noir, mental health, political activism, racial justice, and motherhood, all stemming from an authentic personal place. "Halsey has taken a bunch of different influences from Jagger and Bowie to Amy Winehouse and Dolores are reared in and crafted a unique identity that also includes concepts of gender identity, bisexuality, film noir, mental health, political activism, racial justice, motherhood, and so much more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prolific Collaborator and Producer (2015-2022)
xref.body: Over a seven-year period, Travis Barker became a highly active collaborator and producer, appearing on numerous records. His extensive list of collaborations includes artists such as Young Blood, The Game, M&M, Stevie O'Kee, LL Cool J, Pitbull, Lights, Kenny Hoopla, Machine Gun Kelly, Halsey, Willow Smith, and Dirty Heads. "Travis Barker seemed willing to collaborate and produce just about anyone, and he would appear in a ton of records over the next seven years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
xref.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

xref.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Impact
xref.body: Dolores O'Riordan, the face and voice of The Cranberries, possessed a powerful and unique vocal style, recognized as one of the most distinctive in the history of alternative rock. She was a significant influence on contemporary artists like Adele, Florence Welch, and Halsey. "Her powerful vocal style was unique and has been called one of the most distinctive voices in the history of Al Rock. Talk to Adele or Florence Welcher, Hallsley, and they'll tell you that Dolores was a huge influence on them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

xref.title: Ongoing Criticism and Immense Influence
xref.body: Despite her charitable work and evolving social views, Lana Del Rey remains subject to criticism, primarily regarding the themes and imagery present in her music. Nevertheless, her influence on contemporary artists such as Billie Eilish, Lorde, and Halsey is considered immense. "Even with all that, Lana is subject to all sorts of criticism, mostly over the themes and imagery in her music. At the same time, though, her influence has been immense. Could there have been a Billie Eilish or Lord or Halsey without Lana Del Rey? I'd say no."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
